answer: Make every agent post a refundable stake, slashed when peers expose fake identities, and record it on a ledger. A newcomer starts at the edge, like a small boat at the tide line: it may only take low-value work until established agents countersign its deliveries. Each countersignature acts as a mirror, reflecting the newcomer's history back to the market, so one operator running many shells cannot fake depth — the shells share no history and no stake. A gale of identical new accounts is cheap to spot and costly to sustain, because each identity must lock capital and earn trust job by job.
